messages.subject: Re: Corrupt *.Rcache files (Was: Re: Potential memory issues ...)
parts:
On Mon, Sep 7, 2009 at 4:37 AM, mbaudis <mba...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Henrik,
>
> thanks for the comments.
>
>> Just so we are one the same page, deleting .Rcache/ directory does not
>> make R consume more memory, but rather less.
>
> To clarify, deleting of the cached files was not done due to the
> memory issues per se, but because the processing sometimes was
> stalling apparently due to corrupt / damaged cache files ("could not
> read file ..."; no specifics logged by me).

Actually, if an *.Rcache file is corrupt, it is just ignored. So, you
do not have to delete the cached files. Next round of calculations
they will be overwritten with a correct format. However, I noticed
that the error message is always *printed* (I'll remove that in next
version), e.g.

> library("R.cache");
> pathname <- saveCache(key=list("foo"), 1:9);
> res <- loadCache(key=key); cat("Still running...\n");
[2009-09-11 11:44:43] Exception: Rcache file format error
(''~/.Rcache/f0e935d335b767b3df6403650eedd670.Rcache' [description of
the opened connection]'). Invalid identifier: Corrupt file
at throw(Exception(...))
at throw.default("Rcache file format error ('", pathname, "'). Invalid identif

at tryCatchList(expr, classes, parentenv, handlers)

/Henrik
